Mr. Sanjay Kumar, learned counsel undertakes to file Vakalatnama within 24 hrs. on behalf of revisionist.
3. Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned D.A.G. with Mr. Vipul Painuly and Mr. Bhaskar Chandra Joshi, learned A.G.A. for the State of Uttarakhand/ respondent.

4. By means of the present criminal revision, the revisionist has put to challenge the judgment and order dated 16.09.2021 passed by learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Nainital in Criminal Case No.152 of 2019 State of Uttarakhand Vs. Ajay Agarwal & Another, whereby, the revisionist-Ashok Kumar was convicted under Section 63 read with 31(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 and sentenced six months simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.2,00,000/-, with default stipulation of additional one month's simple imprisonment, as well as the judgment and order dated 18.09.2025 passed by learned Second Additional Sessions Judge, Nainital, in Criminal Appeal No.08 of 2022 Ashok Kumar Vs. State of Uttarakhand & another, whereby, the appeal preferred by revisionist was partly allowed and conviction was affirmed but the sentence was modified from six months s.i. to one month's s.i.
5.

sentences.text:
It is the contended by learned counsel for the revisionist that in Section 63 of the said Act, an amendment has been brought about by amending Act "The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions)
2023", whereby, punishment "with imprisonment for a term may be extend to six months and also with a fine, which may extend to Rs.5,00,000/-" has been amended to "liable to penalty which may extend to Rs.10,00,000/-".

6. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that since amendment has been brought about w.e.f.
11.08.2023, punishment of one month cannot be inflicted upon the revisionist and he can only be inflicted with a fine up to Rs.10,00,000/- for the reason that the amendment is beneficial to the CRLR/633/2025 on 25 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24501285/
1 accused/ revisionist, even if the incident happened prior the date of amendment.
He relied upon certain judgments of Hon'ble Apex court.

7. The incident for which the revisionist was implicated happened on 24.01.2018, therefore, as to whether the provisions of the aforesaid amended Act would be attracted or the earlier provisions of the Act would be attracted, is left open to be argued for learned counsel for the parties.

8. However, in view of the aforesaid submission made by learned counsel for the revisionist, the revisionist is exempted from surrendering before the learned Court concerned, during the pendency of the present criminal revision.
10. Revisionist is directed to deposit 50% of the amount of fine imposed upon him within two months from today.

(Pankaj Purohit, J.) 25.09.2025 PN CRLR/633/2025 on 25 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24501285/
